slides.subtitle: Owner briefing on estate condition, the corpus claim and responsible options
slides.title: RMS estate and language corpus: what is defensible

scqa: The retained database catalogue holds 377199771648 bytes across 1006 tables, with an estimated 259273874 rows. Separate inventories list 143284816848890 bytes in 22975591 objects at OBS, and 47990537059397 bytes in 1456787 files at NAS. A staged audio subset and a separately assembled text corpus have also been measured.

Only 638 table entries were measured, and the census observed 5881277 rows against an estimate of 259273874. The file inventories record custody, not language, music or rights, and they cannot be added together. No final quality receipt exists, so no estate-wide hours or token claim is yet possible.
What can the owner responsibly claim and commercialise today, and what must be done first to widen that claim?

Claim only what is measured: 529.3 hours of staged audio across 3958 files, and 157513 natural text units from 4521 source files. Language identification reached 97.2% conditional macro accuracy on 2800 units, but it is weaker for Kikamba and the Wanga / Luhya label. Complete the coverage ledger and rights review before any licensing, release or revenue statement.
slides.title: The estate is large but only partly measured; a narrow language claim is defensible now
Database estate condition

exhibit.label: Readiness grades of measured relational-table entries only
exhibit.receipt_text: RMS estate census, eij-1b359b3cbd2e; measured 29 September 2026. Exact source hashes in the Word appendix.
exhibit.so_what: Readiness is uneven, so any data product should start from grade A and B tables and treat the rest as remediation work.

slides.title: Grades C and D hold most measured tables; only a minority reach grade A or B

exhibit.label: Database-estate readiness distribution; not speech or text quality
exhibit.receipt_text: RMS estate census, eij-1b359b3cbd2e; measured 29 September 2026. Exact source hashes in the Word appendix.
exhibit.so_what: These grades describe database readiness only; they say nothing about speech or text quality and must not be quoted as corpus quality.

slides.title: Grade C and D tables make up about three in five measured entries; grade E is smallest

points: The catalogue records 377199771648 bytes across 1006 tables, but only 638 table entries were measured and graded.
Estimated rows stand at 259273874; the census observed 5881277, so row-level conclusions rest on a small observed share.
The remaining catalogued tables are ungraded, so no estate-wide grade distribution can be stated.
slides.title: Only part of the catalogue is measured, and observed rows are a small slice of the estimate
File inventories

exhibit.label: Listed storage by separate inventory; not additive unique content
exhibit.receipt_text: OBS and NAS retained listings embedded in the census; 29 September 2026. Metadata scope, not language or music analysis.
exhibit.so_what: The three inventories are separate and cannot be summed into unique content; they show custody scale only.

slides.title: File stores dwarf the database, yet their listings measure bytes, not usable content

points: OBS lists 143284816848890 bytes in 22975591 objects: a retained listing, not an analysis of contents.
NAS lists 47990537059397 bytes in 1456787 files, again scope only, with no language or music labelling.
The inventories may overlap, so no combined unique-content figure should be quoted.
Eligible, non-music, rights-cleared audio inside these stores is unknown until segment-level labels are joined.
slides.title: The two file inventories list large volumes but say nothing yet about language, music or rights
Staged audio

exhibit.label: Measured staged-audio duration by folder label, not certified speech hours
exhibit.receipt_text: Staged-audio header inspection, m9j-3e0dcb1bd16e; verified receipt. Folder labels are not content verification.
exhibit.so_what: Hours are folder-label durations, not certified speech; the two thin labels cannot support model claims without more collection or verification.

slides.title: Six language folders hold similar staged hours; the Wanga and Bukusu labels are thin

exhibit.label: Staged-audio file counts by sample rate; not a quality grade
exhibit.receipt_text: Staged-audio header inspection, m9j-3e0dcb1bd16e; verified receipt. Folder labels are not content verification.
exhibit.so_what: Sample rate is a header property, not a quality grade; it can screen files but cannot certify studio or telephone quality.

slides.title: Most staged files share one sample rate; a sizeable lower-rate group needs screening

exhibit.label: Staged audio and companion transcript inventory; different units by column
exhibit.receipt_text: Staged-audio header inspection, m9j-3e0dcb1bd16e; verified receipt. Folder labels are not content verification.
exhibit.so_what: Pairing by file count is not alignment; transcript accuracy and timing remain unmeasured, and the columns use different units.

slides.title: Transcripts pair with nearly every audio file; the Bukusu folder has none

points: The authorised subset holds 3958 audio files lasting 529.3 hours and occupying 36516920948 bytes.
Companion transcripts number 3939 files and 37192774 bytes, so some audio files have no pair.
Language comes from folder labels, which are not content verification.
Header inspection does not establish speech content, music exclusion or audio quality.
slides.title: The staged set is a labelled subset of real scale, not a verified corpus
Assembled text corpus

exhibit.label: Natural assembled text units by language label
exhibit.receipt_text: RMS transcript assembly, m9j-9a46b862f339; sealed 29 September 2026. Natural units exclude added canaries.
exhibit.so_what: Volume is uneven across languages, so any balanced training or evaluation claim must be stated per language, not pooled.

slides.title: Kalenjin and the Wanga label lead natural text; Kikamba is the thinnest of the seven

exhibit.label: Natural text partition counts; added synthetic canaries excluded
exhibit.receipt_text: RMS transcript assembly, m9j-9a46b862f339; sealed 29 September 2026. Natural units exclude added canaries.
exhibit.so_what: The held-out set is large enough to evaluate against; the archive test is too small to carry conclusions alone. Synthetic canaries are excluded.

slides.title: Most natural text sits in training, with a sizeable held-out set and a very small archive test

exhibit.label: Natural transcript partitions by language label
exhibit.receipt_text: RMS transcript assembly, m9j-9a46b862f339; sealed 29 September 2026. Natural units exclude added canaries.
exhibit.so_what: Partition shape differs by language, so cross-language comparisons should use the held-out set, which exists for all seven.

slides.title: Archive test text sits mainly in Ekegusii and Kikamba; the Wanga label and Kiswahili have none

points: The assembly contains 157513 natural text units; added synthetic canaries are excluded from every count.
The units run to 27329904 characters from 4521 source files; characters are not tokens, and no tokenizer-specific count exists.
Text and audio populations are not joined, so these units are not clean aligned speech-text pairs.
slides.title: The assembled text is a defensible, separately assembled corpus of natural units
Language identification

exhibit.label: Text-ID measured conditional accuracy and coverage on equal strata
exhibit.receipt_text: Text language-ID run, m9j-74af7cef0a85; measured per-stratum results. Not an ASR or general-language certificate.
exhibit.so_what: Conditional accuracy excludes units the tool declined to judge; lower coverage for Kiswahili and the Wanga label means conditional figures flatter real performance.

slides.title: Language-ID is accurate where it judges, but Kikamba and the Wanga label trail the rest

exhibit.label: Text language-ID: conditional accuracy, coverage and correct-of-all; percentages
exhibit.receipt_text: Text language-ID run, m9j-74af7cef0a85; measured per-stratum results. Not an ASR or general-language certificate.
exhibit.so_what: Correct-of-all is the stricter measure and should be quoted beside conditional accuracy, not behind it.

slides.title: Counting every unit, the Wanga label and Kikamba fall furthest, with Kiswahili next

points: The run evaluated 2800 units on equal strata: a per-language sample, not a population estimate.
Conditional macro accuracy is 97.2%, measured only among units the tool chose to judge.
Kikamba and the Wanga label sit clearly below that average, so one headline figure hides the languages needing review.
slides.title: The headline accuracy is high but narrow, and it is not a general-language certificate

points: First, join the inventories of 143284816848890 and 47990537059397 bytes to language, music and rights labels.
Second, complete the census: 638 of 1006 tables are measured; grade the rest before quoting estate condition.
Third, run a rights review of the 529.3 staged hours and 157513 text units before any partner access.
Fourth, verify Bukusu and Wanga labels and review Kikamba identification against human references; publish only the measured claim meanwhile.
slides.title: Build the coverage ledger and clear rights before any external claim

points: Estate-wide non-music eligible audio hours: no joined inventory carries verified labels. The coverage ledger closes this.
Estate-wide text tokens or clean aligned pairs: 377199771648 database bytes are not text volume. Versioned exports and audits close this.
Audio quality and transcript error rates: headers are not quality. Human-reference evaluation closes this.
Licensing, release, savings and revenue: custody is not onward rights. Rights review, invoices and paid pilots close this.
slides.title: Four claims cannot yet be made, each with a defined route to closure

cannot_say.reason: Database storage is not natural-text volume; text and audio populations are not joined

cannot_say.closes_with: Measured observables plus task-specific human-reference evaluation
cannot_say.gap: Studio/telephone quality or transcript error-rate distributions
cannot_say.reason: Header properties do not establish audio quality; no final waveform/annotation certificate
